text:
We will explore some column spaces in this activity.

Consider the matrix $$A= \left[\begin{array}{rrr} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \end{array}\right] = \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 1 \amp 3 \amp -1 \\ -2 \amp 0 \amp -4 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$ Since $\col(A)$ is the span of the columns, we have $$ \col(A) = \laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2,\vvec_3}. $$ Explain why $\vvec_3$ can be written as a linear combination of $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_2$ and why $\col(A)=\laspan{\vvec_1,\vvec_2}$.

Explain why the vectors $\vvec_1$ and $\vvec_2$ form a basis for $\col(A)$ and why $\col(A)$ is a 2-dimensional subspace of $\real^3$ and therefore a plane.

Now consider the matrix $B$ and its reduced row echelon form: $$ B = \left[\begin{array}{rrrr} -2 \amp -4 \amp 0 \amp 6 \\ 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp -3 \\ \end{array}\right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrrr} 1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \amp -3 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array}\right]. $$ Explain why $\col(B)$ is a 1-dimensional subspace of $\real^2$ and is therefore a line.

For a general matrix $A$, what is the relationship between the dimension $\dim~\col(A)$ and the number of pivot positions in $A$?

How does the location of the pivot positions indicate a basis for $\col(A)$?

If $A$ is an invertible $9\times9$ matrix, what can you say about the column space $\col(A)$?

Suppose that $A$ is an $8\times 10$ matrix and that $\col(A) = \real^8$. If $\bvec$ is an 8-dimensional vector, what can you say about the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$?
